text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today after oil prices dropped on news of diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran at the UN. A refiner's profits depend heavily on the spread between crude oil costs and what they can sell refined products for; when oil prices fall sharply—as they did over the past week amid hopes for a Middle East peace deal—that spread often compresses, reducing margins. The stock is down nearly 3% over two weeks as this geopolitical uncertainty has weighed on energy prices.

The timing matters: refineries are running at 96.8% capacity and fuel inventories are substantial, which means there's limited room to benefit from lower input costs if demand doesn't strengthen. Add to that the Trump administration's consideration of a diesel export ban, which would further constrain what refiners can sell into overseas markets and potentially cap upside on any margin recovery.
